shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: I currently have equal quantities (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only A for another B would leave me with 0 A and 2 B, creating imbalance and reducing variety, which lowers my utility given my preference for balanced holdings.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away a B to get an extra A would leave me with 2 A and 0 B, reducing variety and utility since I value having a balanced spread more than an excess of one good. This trade doesn't improve my bundle.

Current inventory is balanced (1,1,1). Trading away my only B for 2 A would leave me with 3 A, 0 B, 1 C - a highly imbalanced bundle that reduces variety, which I value. Rejecting to seek a more balanced trade.
Current inventory is equal (1,1,1). Trading away my only C to get a second B would create imbalance (A:1,B:2,C:0), reducing variety value. Not beneficial.

Trading 1B for 1C would leave me with 1A, 0B, 2C - moving from an even 1-1-1 spread to an unbalanced bundle. Since I value variety and currently have equal amounts of all goods, this trade would reduce my utility by creating an imbalance rather than improving it.

Current inventory is 1/1/1, perfectly balanced. Trading away my only B for 2 C would leave me with 1 A, 0 B, 3 C - creating imbalance and losing variety, which reduces utility given my preference for balanced holdings.
This would leave me with 0 A and 2 B, reducing variety (1,1,1 to 0,2,1). Since I value variety, this trade decreases my utility rather than increasing it.

Trading 1B for 1A would give me 2A, 0B, 1C, creating an imbalanced bundle since I'd have zero B. My current even distribution (1,1,1) is more valuable given my preference for variety, so this trade decreases my utility.

Current inventory is balanced (1,1,1). Trading away my only B for 2 A would leave me with 3 A, 0 B, 1 C - a highly imbalanced bundle that reduces variety value, since I'd have zero of one good. Better to seek a trade that maintains or improves variety.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only C for another B would leave me with 0 C and 2 B, creating an imbalanced bundle that reduces variety value. This doesn't improve my utility.

Trading 1B for 1C would leave me with A:1, B:0, C:2, reducing variety (zero B) which lowers my utility since I value balanced holdings. Current equal bundle (1,1,1) is already balanced, so this swap hurts variety without net gain.

Current inventory is 1A/1B/1C, perfectly balanced. Trading away my only B for 2C would leave me with 1A/0B/3C, creating imbalance (having 0 of B and 3 of C), which reduces variety value even though total goods increase. Better to seek a trade that maintains or improves balance across all three goods.
Trading A(2) for B(1) balances my inventory to A:1,B:2,C:0, improving variety since I have surplus A and deficit B. This increases my utility under a preference for balanced holdings.

I currently have 2 A, 1 B, 0 C. Giving up my only unit of B (my scarcest good besides C) to get more A (already my most abundant good) would worsen my variety balance. This trade decreases utility, so I reject it.

Giving up 2A for 1B would leave me with 0A, 2B, 0C - trading two units of a scarce-to-me good for one unit, and losing all of A entirely. This reduces variety rather than improving it. I'd prefer a more balanced 1-for-1 trade.

I currently have 2 A, 1 B, 0 C. This trade would leave me with 4 A, 0 B, 0 C, making my inventory extremely unbalanced and giving up my only B while gaining more of a good I already have plenty of. This reduces variety and hurts my utility. I'd rather trade B or A for C, or acquire C directly, than stack up further on A.

Current inventory is A:2, B:1, C:0. Giving up my only B (dropping to 0) to get C (going to 1) just swaps which good I have zero of, without improving variety overall. I'd rather keep B and acquire C separately, or trade from A which I have more of.

Giving up my only B would leave me with 0 B, trading variety scarcity for another scarcity. Current: A2,B1,C0. If I accept: A2,B0,C2 - I'd have two goods at 0/2 imbalance similar to before, not a clear improvement. Better to negotiate for only 1 C for 1 B, keeping some B, or get more C without fully depleting B.

Current inventory is A:2, B:0, C:1, heavily skewed away from B. Trading 1 A (which I have surplus of) for 1 B (which I have none of) moves me toward a more even 1-1-1 distribution, increasing my utility given my preference for variety.

Giving up 2 A for only 1 B would leave me with 0 A, 1 B, 1 C - trading a scarce advantage for imbalance. This ratio is too steep; I'd rather get 1 A for 1 B to maintain variety, so I'll decline and counter.

Currently I have A:2, B:0, C:1. Trading away my only C for B would leave me with A:2, B:1, C:0, which just swaps which good I'm missing rather than improving variety. Since I value variety, going from having zero B to zero C doesn't help - I'd rather keep C and try to acquire B without giving up my only C, or find a trade that adds a good without eliminating another.

I currently have equal quantities (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my A for another B would leave me with 0 A, 2 B, 1 C, reducing variety and lowering my utility since I value diversity across goods. No benefit to accept this trade as proposed.

This trade would move me from a balanced (1,1,1) bundle to (2,0,1), reducing variety. Since I value variety and equal distribution, going to 0 in B while having 2 in A decreases my utility rather than increasing it.

Current bundle is balanced at 1/1/1. Accepting would give me 3A/0B/1C, creating a strong imbalance (losing my only B entirely) which reduces variety value more than gaining a third A helps. I'd prefer a trade that keeps some balance, like trading a good I have surplus in rather than my only unit of B.
Current inventory is 1A,1B,1C - perfectly even. Trading 1C for 1B would make me 1A,2B,0C, which is less diverse and gives me a zero holding in C. This decreases my utility since I value variety.

Currently I have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, C. Trading away my B for another C would leave me with 2 C and 0 B, reducing variety and utility. Since I value variety, this trade doesn't improve my bundle.

Current inventory is 1/1/1, a perfectly balanced bundle. Trading away my only B for 2 C would leave me with 1 A, 0 B, 3 C - creating an imbalance (no B at all, excess C) which reduces variety value more than the gain from extra C. I'd prefer a trade that maintains or improves balance across all three goods.
Currently I have 2 A, 0 B, 1 C. Trading 1 A for 1 B moves me to 1 A, 1 B, 1 C, a perfectly balanced bundle which maximizes utility given my preference for variety.

This trade would leave me with 0×A, 1×B, 1×C — trading away all my A for just 1 B is too steep since I'd go from having 2 A to 0, creating a new imbalance. Giving up 2 A for 1 B is not an equal-value trade; I'd rather propose a 1-for-1 swap instead.

This trade would leave me with 0 C and 1 B, just shifting my scarcity from B to C without improving variety. Current bundle: A2,B0,C1. Trading my only C for a B would give A2,B1,C0 - same variety issue, no net gain in diversity. I'd rather keep C and seek a trade that adds B without losing C, e.g. trading A for B.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only A for another B would make my bundle 0 A, 2 B, 1 C, which reduces variety and leaves me with zero of a good. This decreases my utility since I value diversity across goods.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only B for another A would make me have 2×A and 0×B, reducing variety and utility. This trade doesn't improve my bundle balance.

Current bundle is (1,1,1), a balanced set which I value for variety. Trading away my only B for 2 A would leave me with (3,0,1), losing variety and creating a zero-holding, which reduces my utility despite gaining total quantity of A. I'd rather seek a trade that maintains or improves balance.
Current inventory is 1 each of A, B, C, giving balanced variety. Trading away my only C for another B would leave me with 0 C and 2 B, reducing variety and utility. Not beneficial.

Trading away my only B for another C would leave me with 1 A, 0 B, 2 C — moving away from variety, which I value. Since I already have equal amounts (1 each), swapping just shifts imbalance without benefit.

Current bundle is (1,1,1), perfectly balanced. Trading away my only B for 2 C would leave me with (1,0,3), which is less diverse and less valuable given my preference for variety. I'd rather keep balance or trade for something that doesn't zero out a good.

Trading away my only A would leave me with 0 A, 1 B, 2 C - going from having 1 of each of A and B to having 0 A. Currently I have 1 A, 0 B, 2 C. This trade gives me 1 B (going from 0 to 1) but costs me my only A (going from 1 to 0), essentially just swapping which good I have zero of rather than improving variety. Since I value variety, I'd prefer to keep my A and acquire B without giving up A, or find a trade that doesn't zero out a good I already hold.
Currently I have 0 B and 2 C, so trading a surplus C for a scarce B improves variety and balances my bundle to (1,1,1), which is ideal given my equal valuation with diversity preference.

This trade would leave me with A:1, B:1, C:0, trading away all my C for just 1 B. Giving up 2C for 1B is too steep - it would leave me with zero of a good, hurting variety. A better trade would be 1C for 1B to balance my holdings without fully depleting C.

This trade would give me 2×B and 0×A, moving me away from balanced variety (1,1,1) to (0,2,1), which reduces utility since I'd have zero of A. I prefer to maintain diversity across all three goods rather than trade away my only unit of A.

I currently have equal quantities of A, B, and C (1 each). Trading away B for A would just shift the imbalance from A to B without improving variety, resulting in 2 A, 0 B, 1 C, which is less balanced than my current even distribution.

Current inventory is balanced at 1/1/1. Trading away my only B for 2 A would leave me with 3 A, 0 B, 1 C, creating a lopsided bundle and losing variety, which reduces my utility given diminishing value on repeated goods.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only C for another B would leave me with 0 C and 2 B, reducing variety and utility. Since I value variety, this trade would not improve my bundle.
I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only B for another C would leave me with 0 B and 2 C, reducing variety and utility. Not beneficial.

Current inventory is 1/1/1, perfectly balanced. Trading away my only B for 2 C would leave me with 1 A, 0 B, 3 C - highly imbalanced and reducing variety, which hurts my utility since I value variety. I'd rather keep balance or trade for something that maintains it.
Currently I have A:2, B:0, C:1. Trading 1 A for 1 B gives me A:1, B:1, C:1 - a perfectly balanced bundle, which maximizes utility given my preference for variety.

This trade would leave me with 0×A, 1×B, 1×C - going from 2A/0B/1C to 0A/1B/1C. That's still an uneven distribution and gives up too much A (my only surplus good) for just 1 B. I'd rather trade only 1×A for 1×B to balance my inventory to 1A/1B/1C, which maximizes variety value.

I currently have 0 B and 1 C, so C is not abundant enough to give up for equal value; this trade would leave me with 0 C and 1 B, just shifting scarcity rather than improving variety. Since I have 2 A, 0 B, 1 C, trading C away to get B would make me have A:2, B:1, C:0, which still leaves one good at zero. Better to seek a trade that raises my minimum holdings without zeroing out another good, e.g., trading A instead of C.
